introduction: Tailored for the highest conceptual tiers of NEET, this level handles the complex processes of secondary growth in dicots (wood formation) and dissects the intricate anatomical and physiological systems of model organisms: the Cockroach and the Frog.

core_concepts.title: Secondary Growth in Dicot Stems
core_concepts.description:
Increase in girth caused by two lateral meristems: 
1. Vascular Cambium: Forms a continuous ring. It cuts off new cells on both sides. Inner cells differentiate into Secondary Xylem (Wood), and outer cells differentiate into Secondary Phloem. Secondary xylem accumulates heavily, crushing primary/secondary phloem.
2. Cork Cambium (Phellogen): Formed in the cortex to replace the broken outer epidermis. It cuts off Cork (Phellem) on the outside (suberized, dead) and Secondary Cortex (Phelloderm) on the inside. 
Phellogen + Phellem + Phelloderm = Periderm.

core_concepts.title: Heartwood vs. Sapwood (Spring vs. Autumn Wood)
core_concepts.description:
- Spring/Early Wood vs. Autumn/Late Wood: Activity of cambium depends on the season. Spring wood has wider vessels (lighter color); Autumn wood has narrow vessels (darker color). The two together make one Annual Ring.
- Heartwood vs. Sapwood: Heartwood is the central, dark, dead secondary xylem filled with tannins, resins, and essential oils. It provides mechanical support but DOES NOT conduct water. Sapwood is the peripheral, lighter, living secondary xylem involved in the conduction of water and minerals.

core_concepts.title: Morphology & Anatomy of Cockroach (Periplaneta americana)
core_concepts.description:
- Exoskeleton: Chitinous plates called sclerites (tergites dorsal, sternites ventral), joined by a flexible articular membrane (arthrodial membrane).
- Digestive System: Foregut includes Crop (storing food) and Gizzard/Proventriculus (grinding food). Hepatic Caeca (6-8 blind tubules) at the foregut/midgut junction secrete digestive juices.
- Excretory System: Malpighian Tubules (100-150 yellow tubules) at the midgut/hindgut junction absorb nitrogenous waste (uricotelic).
- Circulatory System: Open type. 13-chambered heart with ostia.
- Vision: Compound eyes containing ~2000 hexagonal ommatidia, providing mosaic vision (high sensitivity, low resolution).

core_concepts.title: Morphology & Anatomy of Frog (Rana tigrina)
core_concepts.description:
- Respiration: Cutaneous (through moist skin) in water/hibernation. Pulmonary (lungs) and Buccopharyngeal cavity on land.
- Circulatory System: 3-chambered heart (2 atria, 1 ventricle). Presence of Sinus venosus (receives blood through vena cava) and Conus arteriosus (truncus arteriosus).
- Excretory & Reproductive System: Frogs are ureotelic. In males, the excretory and reproductive tracts merge into a common Urogenital Tract that opens into the Cloaca. The Cloaca is a small, median chamber that passes fecal matter, urine, and sperms to the exterior.

important_entities.name: Bark and Lenticels
important_entities.key_fact: Bark is a non-technical term for all tissues exterior to the vascular cambium.
important_entities.significance: Bark includes both the Periderm (Cork, Cork Cambium, Sec. Cortex) AND the Secondary Phloem. Lenticels are lens-shaped openings in the periderm where the cork cambium produces loosely arranged parenchyma cells (complementary cells) instead of thick cork cells. Lenticels permit the exchange of gases between the outer atmosphere and the internal tissues of the stem.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Malpighian Tubules vs. Hepatic Caeca Location
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
Examiners frequently swap these locations in multiple-choice questions to trap students. 
- Hepatic Caeca (Digestive juice secretion) = Junction of Foregut and Midgut.
- Malpighian Tubules (Excretion of Uric acid) = Junction of Midgut and Hindgut.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Labrum is the Upper Lip, Labium is the Lower Lip
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: To avoid confusing the two: Lab**rum** (has a 'u' for **U**pper lip). Lab**ium** (has an 'l' for **L**ower lip). The Hypopharynx acts as the tongue.

exam_strategy_tips: In frog anatomy, remember that males possess vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimbs, which are totally absent in female frogs. This sexual dimorphism is a frequently tested fact.
